title: Screed a paver sand bed flat with a board riding on two steel rails
instruction: Take the screed board off its rest blocks, lay it across the two rails at the far end, and pull it toward you so it shaves the bedding sand down to the rail tops. Then set the board back on its rest blocks and leave the bed untouched.
context: Paver crews (construction laborers and landscaping workers) screed the bedding sand under every patio, walkway and repair patch before a paver goes down. The board comes off the trestle, lies across two rails set at the bed thickness inside the edging, and is pulled toward the worker with both hands in step, shaving the high sand into a ridge ahead of it and dragging the ridge into hollows. If one end lags it skews, if it lifts it skims and leaves a hump, if it stops it digs a trench; the pavers then rock and lip, a trip edge, and the bed is raked and screeded again. Footprints or a tool pressed into the finished sand mean the same rework. The board goes back on the trestle; pulling the rails and filling their trenches is a later, separate job.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top (TOP) is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. All of this stands on the table. (1) Edging: three fixed grey steel flats, 25 mm thick and 60 mm tall: the far one at x 415 to 440 mm (y -215 to +215 mm) and one each side at y +215 to +240 mm and y -240 to -215 mm (x 200 to 440 mm). The near side (x 200 mm) is open. (2) Two fixed orange steel square tubes, 25 x 25 mm, 215 mm long along x (x 200 to 415 mm), centred at y +112.5 and -112.5 mm: the rails, tops 25 mm above TOP (the bedding thickness). (3) Bedding sand (play sand, about 1.5 g/mL), a bulk model: 25 mm cells, 8 along x (x 200 to 400 mm) by 16 along y (y -200 to +200 mm); the 2 columns under the rails are steel, so 112 are sand. A 20 mm tan slab is drawn under the sand; the sand's depth is kept by the scorer. Depth is measured from TOP. Start depths: 36 mm everywhere; 25 mm in the column x 375 to 400 mm (the board starts over it) and in the 15 mm strips beside each wall (out of the board's reach, not scored); a mound of 3 x 3 cells at 45 mm (x 300 to 375 mm, y -100 to -25 mm); a hollow of 3 x 3 cells at 19 mm (x 225 to 300 mm, y 0 to +75 mm). About 3.6 kg in the 112 cells. (4) The screed board: a loose aluminium rectangular tube, 25 mm wide (x) by 50 mm tall, 1.5 mm wall, 400 mm long along y, 0.24 kg, on edge, so its 25 mm face is the sole. It starts on two fixed dark steel rest blocks (a pair of trestles), each 40 x 30 x 55 mm, at x 130 to 170 mm, one at y +125 to +155 mm and one at y -155 to -125 mm, tops 55 mm above TOP; the board is centred at x 150 mm, y 0, its ends 45 mm past the blocks. The job: fetch the board; lay it across both rails with its centre at x 387.5 mm (sole over the last cell column, 15 mm from the far wall); pull it 175 mm toward the robot with its sole on the rail tops and both ends in step; lift it clear and set it back on the blocks. Resting on the rails the sole is at 25 mm, so the sand under it is cut to 25 mm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial and keeps the sand's depth in every cell (see fidelity). 'Bridged pull': on every step of a run the board's underside is within 3 mm of both rail tops where its centre line crosses them, and its centre travels at least 150 mm along x in that run. 'Cut': at least 84 of the 112 sand cells (three quarters) within 6 mm of 25 mm. 'Deviation': the largest |depth - 25 mm| over all 112 sand cells (every cell, not a sample). 'Stowed': the board's underside is within 3 mm of both rest-block tops, its centre within 10 mm of the blocks' centre line, turned under 3 degrees about z and tilted under 3 degrees. 'Hands off': on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones (the pads and a 56 mm radius round them when open, 16 mm when closed) are 30 mm or more from the board, the rails and the bed; 'still': over that second the board moves under 1 mm and turns under 0.3 degrees. 'Pressed': after the board has passed a cell (its sole was on that cell's sand and has moved on), a pad tip, or any part of a board tilted more than 30 degrees (on its side or flat: it cuts nothing), came within 2 mm of that cell's sand or into it, until the board passes it again. Score 0 if the board's lowest point ever goes 20 mm below the table top (knocked off the table), or without a bridged pull, or without 'cut' (doing nothing scores 0: 23 cells are within 6 mm at the start). Otherwise: 1.0 deviation 3 mm or less, board stowed, hands off and still; 0.75 deviation 4 mm or less and board stowed; 0.5 deviation 6 mm or less; 0.25 otherwise. Pressed caps any score at 0.5. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. There is no zero gate for rework: the harm here is rework, not injury. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, per condition: bridged, a side video along each rail, level with its top, a 3 mm gauge block on the rail for scale and a tape beside it: the gap under the sole stays below the block on every frame of a 150 mm run; cut and deviation, lay a straightedge across the two side walls (tops 60 mm) and read the gap to the sand with a depth gauge at the 112 cell centres (depth = 60 mm minus gap), or lay it on both rail tops at each 25 mm step along x and slide a 3, 4 or 6 mm feeler under it along its length; stowed, a 3 mm feeler under the board at each block and a square for 3 degrees; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and a dial indicator on the board; pressed, look for footprints or a tool mark in the finished sand.
reset_notes: Rake the sand to 36 mm, then build the mound (3 x 3 cells, 45 mm) and press the hollow (3 x 3 cells, 19 mm) with a depth gauge on a straightedge across the side walls; strike the column x 375 to 400 mm and the 15 mm strips beside the walls to 25 mm with the board on the rails. Check both rails are square to the edging with tops 25 mm above the table. Set the board on its blocks, centred at x 150 mm. Use damp play sand; rake it level between runs.
fidelity: Sand is a height model on 25 mm cells kept by the scorer from the board's measured pose; a 20 mm slab is drawn. Cut and fill is contact driven: sand above the sole (tilt and skew count) is cut into a heap carried in its column; lower cells are filled from it while the board rides within 3 mm of the rails; a lifted board drops it ahead; heap past the near edge is lost. No sand drag on the board. The tube is a solid box of its real mass. Friction is the simulator default.
